newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended firmer on Wednesday after a midsession dip, but the lack of buying on a thin day left a number of traders questioning the potential for further market strides.
Strengthening U.S. treasuries provided a much-needed boost after a midsession when the lack of buying exposed market nerves and brought prices sharply back from opening gains.

"It's been quite strong again. But unlike yesterday, when there were a lot of buyers, especially in the long end, today it's really just sellers. There are certainly no domestic buyers," one trader said.
Short-dated paper, particularly 1998, was well-offered. Traders were uncertain whether the offers were outright sales or linked to unwinding of swaps positions.
Long-dated issues, from Jan 2006, strengthened as liquidity remained poor and traders needed to cover minor shorts.
"Jan 2006 was bought reasonably aggressively early in the morning and late in the day," one trader said.
Traders commented that the rejection of a move downwards early in the afternoon provided slightly positive signals, but few believed there were much scope for significant gains.
Thin volumes and poor buying did not bode well, they said.
"I don't know that it's a market that can really hold strong," one trader said.
